### Day 11: 1 Samuel 9:14b–25
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-11-1-samuel-9-14b25.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 9:14b-25
Points:
- Saul appeared physically impressive, yet he struggled with deep-seated insecurity and a poor self-concept.
- When told of the honor awaiting him, Saul immediately focused on his small tribe and lowly clan.
- Low self-esteem is not true humility; both self-exaltation and self-denigration keep the self at the center.
- Godly humility directs attention away from personal status and fixes it entirely on the Master.
- True spiritual confidence comes not from self-reliance, but from resting in an almighty God.

### Samuel Meets Saul
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/samuel-meets-saul
Passage: 1 Samuel 9:3-27
Points:
- God's providence governs every detail, using lost donkeys and unexpected detours to guide Saul to Samuel.
- Events that appear to be mere coincidences are often the Lord silently directing our steps.
- Although Israel sought a king for worldly reasons, God showed mercy because He heard His people crying out.
- God revealed His plan beforehand to Samuel, confirming that circumstances unfold according to His sovereign decree.
- Believers can trust God amid life's disappointments and disrupted plans, knowing He directs all things for good.

### Devotional: 1 Samuel 9
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/1-samuel-9-romans-7-jeremiah-46-psalm-22/
Passage: 1 Samuel 9:1-27
Points:
- Saul began his journey with great promise and modest humility, yet a good start does not guarantee a good finish.
- Believers who experience early success must remain watchful, persevering in small acts of daily faithfulness.
- Human judgment regarding future leadership is fallible, as people can change drastically over time.
- God's people need biblical mechanisms of accountability for leaders who turn out to be unfaithful.
- Because only the Lord knows the end from the beginning, we must place our full trust in His Word.
